title: EIP-8491: LUCID Key Publisher Priority Lists
description: Extend EIP-8184 with validator-selected key publisher priority and authenticated key release
author: Jannik Luhn (@jannikluhn)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP extends [EIP-8184](./eip-8184.md) with a validator-managed priority list of key publishers. Sealed transactions using publishers on this list execute before other sealed transactions, mitigating the impact of key publishers' optionality over key release. Publishers are included on the list when supported by more than half of active validator effective balance. ## Motivation In LUCID, key publishers can choose whether to release a committed transaction's decryption key after learning how later transactions would execute. This optionality can enable frontrunning even when those later transactions are encrypted. Giving execution priority to transactions whose key publishers the validator set deems trusted prevents transactions using other publishers from exploiting selective key release to execute ahead of them. ## Specification ### Additional constants and parameters ```python LUCID_KEY_MESSAGE_PREFIX = b"LUCID_KEY_MESSAGE" MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_ADDRESSES_PER_LIST = TBD MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_LISTS = TBD MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD = TBD TARGET_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD = TBD MIN_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REQUEST_FEE = TBD KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REQUEST_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION = TBD KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_SYSTEM_CALL_GAS_LIMIT = TBD SYSTEM_ADDRESS = 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REGISTRY_ADDRESS = TBD DOMAIN_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_SUBSCRIPTION = TBD KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REQUEST_TYPE = TBD ``` ### Key publisher voting Validators vote for key publishers by subscribing to lists of execution addresses. Each list is managed by an owner through a registry contract on the execution layer. Each active validator contributes its full effective balance to every address in its subscribed list. An address has priority when its support exceeds half of the total effective balance of all active validators. #### Beacon state and priority list The beacon state is extended with key publisher vote lists, validator subscriptions to those lists, and subscription nonces: ```python VoteListIndex = uint64 class BeaconState(Container): ... key_publisher_vote_list_addresses: List[List[ExecutionAddress, MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_ADDRESSES_PER_LIST], MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_LISTS] key_publisher_vote_subscriptions: List[Union[None, VoteListIndex], VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_LIMIT] key_publisher_vote_subscription_nonces: List[uint64, VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_LIMIT] ``` For slot $n$, let $P_n$ be the priority list derived from the beacon state after all block, slot, and epoch processing through slot $n-1$, including any skipped slots, and before processing slot $n$ or its beacon block. An ST has priority in slot $n$ if its ticket's `key_publisher` is in $P_n$. All STs in a bundle have the same `key_publisher`, so each ST-commitment has one priority status. The derivation of $P_n$ is specified under "Key publisher voting". #### Registry contract The registry contract is deployed at `KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_REGISTRY_ADDRESS`. Anyone may create an empty list, initially owned by its creator. List IDs are assigned consecutively in creation order, starting at zero. IDs are never reused, and lists cannot be deleted. The contract rejects creation when the number of lists already created equals `MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_VOTE_LISTS`. A list's owner may add or remove addresses or transfer ownership. Lists are unordered sets of distinct addresses: adding an existing address or removing an absent address does not change list membership. The list-management interface defines the operations and their corresponding events: ```solidity interface IKeyPublisherVoteLists { event ListCreated(uint64 indexed listId, address indexed owner); event AddressesAdded(uint64 indexed listId, address[] addresses); event AddressesRemoved(uint64 indexed listId, address[] addresses); event OwnershipTransferred( uint64 indexed listId, address indexed previousOwner, address indexed newOwner ); function createList() external payable returns (uint64 listId); function addAddresses(uint64 listId, address[] calldata addresses) external payable; function removeAddresses(uint64 listId, address[] calldata addresses) external payable; function transferOwnership(uint64 listId, address newOwner) external; } ``` The contract rejects an add, remove, or ownership-transfer call unless the list exists and the caller is its current owner. Each accepted add/remove call contains at most `MAX_KEY_PUBLISHER_ADDRESSES_PER_LIST` addresses, counting duplicates toward this input bound. An accepted addition leaves at most that many distinct addresses in the complete list. Calls exceeding either bound revert atomically. Successful list-management calls immediately update the execution-layer registry. Creation, addition, and removal calls are subject to the fee specified under "Request fee". #### Validator subscriptions Anyone may relay a validator subscription through the registry contract. The signed message uses the following SSZ containers: ```python class KeyPublisherVoteSubscription(Container): validator_index: ValidatorIndex list_id: VoteListIndex nonce: uint64 class SignedKeyPublisherVoteSubscription(Container): message: KeyPublisherVoteSubscription signature: BLSSignature ``` The subscription interface accepts individual fields and emits them in `VoteSubscriptionSubmitted`: ```solidity interface IKeyPublisherVoteSubscriptions { event VoteSubscriptionSubmitted( uint64 indexed validatorIndex, uint64 indexed listId, uint64 nonce, bytes signature ); function submitVoteSubscription( uint64 validatorIndex, uint64 listId, uint64 nonce, bytes calldata signature ) external payable; } ``` The contract requires an existing execution-layer list and a signature of exactly 96 bytes. It accepts the fields of a `SignedKeyPublisherVoteSubscription` without verifying the signature, validator index, or nonce, and does not maintain validator subscriptions.
